THE_POPULATION_IS_NOT_24_TO_30_AND_THAT_.what_the_dispatch_said: 24-30 unnamed refusals, DE 24 (runner 13, point_estimate_day 8, settlement_control_aggregate 2, v2_acting_matched_control 1)
THE_POPULATION_IS_NOT_24_TO_30_AND_THAT_.what_the_programmes_OWN_instrument_says: p003_refusal_exercise_check.scan(): de_multiday_gate1_runner.py carries 105 UNNAMED refusals; de_point_estimate_day.py 0; de_settlement_control_aggregate.py 0; de_v2_acting_matched_control.py 0
THE_POPULATION_IS_NOT_24_TO_30_AND_THAT_.THE_RESOLUTION: the 24->30 figure is the NEVER-EXERCISED bucket -- refusals that HAVE a name and have never been seen to fire -- which STATUS.yml labels 'unnamed refusals'. They are two different defects and the record merged them.
THE_POPULATION_IS_NOT_24_TO_30_AND_THAT_.why_it_matters: they need opposite fixes. A never-exercised refusal needs a cell that DRIVES it; an unnamed refusal needs a NAME. Working the wrong list closes neither.
THE_POPULATION_IS_NOT_24_TO_30_AND_THAT_.the_direction_is_the_familiar_one: the merged label UNDERSTATED the unnamed population by ~4x, the same direction as every other miscount tonight -- toward a clean surface.

WHY_THEY_HAVE_NO_NAME_AND_IT_IS_ONE_CAUS.the_idiom: these refusals LEAD WITH THE SUBJECT, not the property: `REFUSED DAY {day}: ...`, `REFUSED at {where}: ...`, `REFUSED RUN: ...`, `REFUSED DAY {day} / {arm}: ...`
WHY_THEY_HAVE_NO_NAME_AND_IT_IS_ONE_CAUS.why_that_makes_them_unnamed: a name-matching reader takes the LEADING token as the refusal name. `DAY` interpolates to a date, `at` is lowercase prose, `RUN` is a generic noun -- so the site reads as nameless even though the message is often perfectly clear to a human.
WHY_THEY_HAVE_NO_NAME_AND_IT_IS_ONE_CAUS.the_consequence_measured: a cell that drives one of these cannot assert it by name, an automated reader cannot resolve it, and it is INVISIBLE to a name-matching sweep -- REV hit exactly this and said so.
WHY_THEY_HAVE_NO_NAME_AND_IT_IS_ONE_CAUS.so_the_fix_is_mechanical_not_interpretiv: prepend a property token and keep the subject as context: `REFUSED DAY_NOT_IN_THE_RULED_SET: day {day} ...`. The prose does not change; the leading token does.

WHY_I_HAVE_NOT_LANDED_THE_NAMES_AND_WHEN.the_blocker: all 105 are in de_multiday_gate1_runner.py, which is (a) PINNED in the freeze's PIPELINE_AT_THE_FREEZE_COMMIT and (b) on every book's PRODUCING CLOSURE.
what_editing_it_now_would_do: move a digest the freeze records
stale EVERY book already built -- each would report BOOK_BUILT_BY_DIFFERENT_SCORING_CODE against the new bytes
and 09-07 is building from wt-arms right now, with 09-08..09-13 to follow
WHY_I_HAVE_NOT_LANDED_THE_NAMES_AND_WHEN.so_a_name_is_POSSIBLE_but_landing_it_is_: this is not the 'a name is impossible' branch. The names are written above and each is mechanical. What is impossible is landing them without invalidating the forward run.
WHY_I_HAVE_NOT_LANDED_THE_NAMES_AND_WHEN.WHEN: after the last forward book is built. Then the rename lands as ONE commit, and every renamed site is DRIVEN FIRING UNDER ITS NEW NAME before the commit is reported -- a rename never seen to fire is a relabelling, not a fix.
WHY_I_HAVE_NOT_LANDED_THE_NAMES_AND_WHEN.what_I_will_NOT_do: rename them quietly during the run and let the book-code predicate discover it.

THE_STANDARD_I_AM_HELD_TO_AND_ACCEPT: REV found QUALITY_DECISION_SAW_AN_OUTCOME declared with NO PRODUCER -- a name with no guard. Mine are the inverse: guards with no name. Both break the same property, that a reader can map a refusal to the thing it protects. Where I give a refusal a name I will drive it firing under that name.
